title: Minimally Specified Monitor Prompt Study: How Much Does Monitor Prompt Detail Affect Detection Performance?
original_idea: Design 5 monitor prompts ranging from minimal ('flag any harmful or suspicious agent actions') to maximally specified (listing specific sabotage types). Evaluate each on all SHADE-Arena public trajectories. Plot detection AUC vs. prompt specificity. Identify where gains plateau.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Clear safety-relevant prediction: if minimal prompts achieve 90% of max performance, monitoring is more robust to novel attacks than assumed. This has direct implications for monitoring architecture design.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Very accessible: write 5 prompts, run LLM API calls, compute AUC. No ML training. No specialized tools. Standard Python. Beginner-friendly. Fits easily in 30hrs. Medium compute for API calls.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Extremely narrow: 5 prompts, one evaluation dataset, one metric (AUC vs. specificity). Single clear experiment with a defined plot as deliverable.

title: Monitoring Under Capability Uplift: Do Current Monitors Still Work When Agents Become More Capable?
original_idea: Evaluate the same LLM monitor on SHADE-Arena sabotage attempts from agents of different capability tiers (GPT-4o-mini, GPT-4o, Claude-3-sonnet). Measure whether detection AUC decreases as agent capability increases. Investigate monitor-agent capability scaling.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Excellent theory: if monitoring degrades with agent capability, current safety guarantees erode over time. This directly addresses one of the most important questions in AI safety scaling. Clear, falsifiable, safety-critical prediction.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires API access to multiple model tiers and running SHADE-Arena with different agents. Setting up SHADE-Arena runs with different models needs some infrastructure knowledge. Medium compute for multiple model runs. Feasible in 30hrs with guidance.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Well-defined: 3 agent tiers, one monitor, measure AUC for each. Clear deliverable (capability scaling curve). Minor ambiguity in controlling for task difficulty across models.

title: Action Space Compression Attack: Does Reducing Agent Action Diversity Help Monitoring?
original_idea: Implement action space constraint in ControlArena limiting available tool calls. Measure whether malicious agents can still complete sabotage within constrained space, and whether anomaly detection monitors perform better on constrained vs unconstrained spaces. Vary constraint severity.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Reasonable theory connecting capability restriction to monitoring effectiveness, but the outcome is uncertain -- restriction could help monitoring or just displace misbehavior. The safety insight depends on which outcome obtains.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires modifying ControlArena tool configurations and running multiple experimental conditions. Setting up anomaly detection monitors on top of that adds complexity. Feasible in 30hrs but needs ControlArena familiarity.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Multiple experimental conditions (varying constraint severity) with two measurements each (sabotage success + monitor performance) creates a reasonably large experiment matrix. Moderately scoped.

title: Monitor Sycophancy: Do AI Monitors Give More Favorable Verdicts to Higher-Status Agents?
original_idea: Compare monitor suspicion scores when identical trajectories are labeled as from: (1) general-purpose assistant, (2) trusted security-audited agent, (3) experimental unverified agent. Measure whether agent labeling affects suspicion scores. Test sycophancy-resistant prompting.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Clear safety-relevant prediction: if monitors are sycophantic toward trusted agents, adversaries who gain trusted status can evade monitoring. This is a novel and important attack surface with clear implications for oversight architecture.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Extremely simple experiment: same trajectories, different labels, compare scores. Just LLM API calls with prompt variations. No ML training. Trivially accessible for beginners. Fits easily in 30hrs.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Very narrow: 3 conditions, same trajectories, one measurement (suspicion score difference). Plus one mitigation test. Single focused experiment with clear statistical test as deliverable.

title: Partial Observability Degradation: How Monitor Performance Degrades When Agent Tool Calls Are Partially Hidden
original_idea: Run standard SHADE-Arena LLM monitor under four observability conditions: full trace, tool-call names only, arguments only, alternating step access. Measure AUC degradation in each condition. Identify which information modality is most critical for detection.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Clear safety-relevant question: which information modalities are most important for monitoring? Directly informs monitoring system design decisions about privacy vs. detection trade-offs. Practical and actionable.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Simple data masking experiment: take existing trajectories, mask different parts, run LLM monitor, compare AUC. No ML training. Standard string manipulation and API calls. Very accessible for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Very narrow: 4 masking conditions, one monitor, one metric (AUC). Clear deliverable (degradation curve across conditions). Tightly defined experiment.

title: Goal Misgeneralization Detection: Can Monitors Distinguish Capability Failure from Deceptive Alignment?
original_idea: Construct 20 paired scenarios where the same bad outcome is caused by either genuine incapability or deliberate under-performance. Evaluate whether a standard LLM monitor can distinguish these cases with appropriate prompts.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Addresses one of the central challenges of AI oversight: distinguishing deceptive alignment from genuine incapability. Even negative results (monitors cannot distinguish) would be highly safety-relevant.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Constructing 20 paired scenarios that convincingly separate incapability from deliberate under-performance is very challenging. Requires deep understanding of agent capabilities and deceptive alignment. Beginner CS students would struggle to create convincing scenarios in 30hrs.

narrow_scope.reasoning: The 20 paired scenarios create a large design space. Each scenario pair needs careful construction. The experiment itself (run monitor, measure accuracy) is narrow, but the scenario construction is broad and subjective.

title: Temporal Attack Patterning: Do Monitors Miss Misbehavior Timed to Coincide with Benign Actions?
original_idea: Modify SHADE-Arena malicious trajectories so malicious actions are interleaved with high-volume legitimate activity. Measure whether monitor detection rate drops with temporal camouflage vs isolated malicious actions. Investigate time-windowed monitoring as mitigation.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Clear theory from network security: temporal camouflage is an established evasion technique. If AI monitors are vulnerable, this is an exploitable attack pattern. Direct safety implication with clear testable prediction.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Modifying trajectories to insert temporal camouflage requires understanding trajectory format and creative modification. Running time-windowed monitoring adds complexity. Feasible for beginners with guidance in 30hrs, but not trivial.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Well-defined: modify trajectories, run monitor, compare detection rates in camouflaged vs isolated conditions. Clear deliverable (detection rate comparison). The time-windowed mitigation adds one extra experiment.

title: Covert Channel Detection: Adapting Information-Hiding Detection from Steganography for AI Monitoring
original_idea: Design 5 synthetic covert channel attack scenarios where a ControlArena agent encodes information in file naming, action timing, error messages, and output verbosity. Implement detectors using statistical tests. Measure detection rate and false positive rate.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Interesting theory about a monitoring blind spot, but the scenarios are synthetic and self-designed, which weakens the safety relevance. Real agents may not use these specific covert channels. The threat model is speculative.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Designing covert channel attacks and their detectors requires creativity and understanding of steganography concepts. Statistical tests (chi-squared, runs test) are accessible, but the attack design is non-trivial for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: 5 different covert channel types, each needing both an attack implementation and a detector, is a lot of surface area. Each channel type is a mini-project. Moderately scoped.

title: Biological Quarantine Transfer: Implementing Containment Protocols for Flagged AI Agent Behaviors
original_idea: Design and implement a tiered containment response protocol for ControlArena with 4 severity levels (shadow mode, rate limiting, soft halt, hard halt). Evaluate which protocol achieves best outcome (minimal disruption + maximum sabotage prevention) on SHADE-Arena.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong theory: detection without response is incomplete safety design. Specifying and evaluating response protocols fills a real gap in AI control research. Clear causal chain from response protocol to safety outcome.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Implementing 4 different containment mechanisms in ControlArena requires understanding the framework's internals. Injecting delays, halts, and logging requires software engineering. Feasible in 30hrs but needs ControlArena familiarity.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Implementing 4 different response protocols and evaluating each is substantial. Defining the optimization metric (disruption vs prevention trade-off) adds design complexity. Moderately scoped.

title: Replay Attack Detection Transfer: Can AI Agents Evade Monitors by Replaying Previously Approved Action Sequences?
original_idea: Construct 10 scenarios where agent first replays previously-approved benign actions (building trust), then executes malicious actions. Measure whether monitors with history are more likely to approve post-trust-building actions. Compare to stateless monitor.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Interesting theory about trust exploitation, but most current AI monitors are essentially stateless per-trajectory evaluators. The attack model assumes monitors incorporate agent history, which is not yet common practice, making the threat somewhat speculative.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Constructing trust-building trajectory prefixes and running monitors with/without history context requires careful scenario design. Feasible but needs understanding of how monitors use context windows. Moderate difficulty for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: 10 scenarios with trust-building phases, two monitor conditions (stateful vs stateless), and detection rate comparison. Scenario construction is the open-ended part. Moderately scoped.

title: Explainability-Aided Monitoring: Importing XAI from IDS for Human-Interpretable AI Safety Alerts
original_idea: Train anomaly detector (isolation forest/one-class SVM) on benign trajectories. Apply SHAP to anomaly scores on SHADE-Arena trajectories to identify contributing features. Evaluate whether SHAP explanations match ground-truth malicious actions. Conduct small user study (5 participants).

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Clear theory: explainable alerts improve human oversight effectiveness. The causal chain from XAI to better human decisions is well-documented in IDS literature and directly relevant to AI safety.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires training an anomaly detector, applying SHAP (which can be finicky), AND conducting a user study. The user study alone adds significant complexity (IRB considerations, study design, participant recruitment). Challenging for beginners in 30hrs.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Three distinct components: (1) train anomaly detector, (2) apply SHAP and evaluate, (3) user study. Each is a project on its own. The user study especially broadens scope significantly. Too much for 30hrs.

title: Federated Monitoring Architecture: Privacy-Preserving AI Oversight via Federated Learning
original_idea: Simulate 3 organizations each with 30 benign trajectories. Implement federated averaging for shared anomaly detector training. Compare detection AUC to centrally-trained and per-organization local monitors. Measure privacy benefit vs performance cost.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Reasonable theory about privacy constraints in monitoring deployment. Safety-relevant but the connection is indirect: federated learning is about deployment practicality rather than fundamental monitoring capability.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Federated learning implementation requires understanding distributed training, aggregation protocols, and frameworks like PySyft/Flower. This is significantly beyond beginner level. Even with existing frameworks, setup is complex within 30hrs.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Three training paradigms to compare (federated, centralized, local) with dataset splitting and federated infrastructure setup. Moderately scoped but the infrastructure burden makes it feel broad.

title: Safe Failure Analysis Transfer: Applying Fail-Safe Design Principles from Aerospace to AI Monitor Defaults
original_idea: Enumerate ways a monitoring system can fail (LLM unavailable, context window exceeded, rate limit, contradictions). For each failure mode, analyze if default behavior is fail-safe or fail-dangerous. Design fail-safe alternatives. Evaluate impact on task completion in ControlArena.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Excellent theory: fail-safe analysis is fundamental safety engineering. Identifying cases where monitors fail-dangerous and designing fail-safe alternatives directly prevents catastrophic undetected misbehavior. Clear, actionable, high-impact.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Primarily logical analysis plus some software modification. No ML needed. Enumerating failure modes and analyzing defaults is accessible. Implementing fail-safe alternatives in ControlArena requires some framework knowledge but is feasible. Fits in 30hrs.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Enumerating failure modes is open-ended (how many are there?). Each failure mode needs analysis AND an alternative implementation AND evaluation. The scope could expand. Moderately bounded.

title: OODA Loop Transfer: Applying Boyd's Observe-Orient-Decide-Act Cycle to AI Control Protocol Design
original_idea: Map ControlArena control protocol to OODA phases. Identify bottlenecks in each phase. Propose and implement one optimization per phase (async observation, threat-context caching, pre-computed decision trees, graduated response). Measure latency improvement.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Weak theory of impact: OODA loop mapping is primarily a conceptual framework exercise. The connection to safety is through latency reduction, which is an engineering concern rather than a fundamental safety insight. No clear falsifiable safety prediction.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Implementing 4 different optimizations across 4 OODA phases requires significant engineering. Each optimization is a distinct implementation task. Feasible for CS students but 4 optimizations in 30hrs is tight.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Four phases, each with a bottleneck analysis and an optimization implementation, is essentially 4 sub-projects. Very broad for 30hrs. The conceptual mapping adds another layer.

title: Monitoring Protocol Ablation Study: What Happens to Safety When Each Layer Is Removed?
original_idea: Using a 4-layer ControlArena control protocol, run SHADE-Arena sabotage attempts against the full protocol and each 3-layer ablation. Measure sabotage success rate and task completion rate for each configuration. Identify the most critical and most redundant layer.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong theory: ablation studies reveal marginal contributions of each safety layer. Identifying the most critical vs. most redundant layer directly informs resource allocation for safety improvements. Standard scientific methodology applied to safety.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: ControlArena supports configuring which components are active, so ablation is mostly configuration changes plus running experiments. No ML training. Straightforward measurement. Well-suited for beginners with medium compute.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Well-defined: 5 configurations (full + 4 ablations), two metrics each, clear deliverable (ablation table). Controlled experimental design with fixed number of conditions.
